title: Migration 43 — MFA for gate approval
description: Applies migrations 39-43, runs 43's VERIFY A-G, then rolls back 43 on a disposable PostgreSQL 18 cluster. Plan section 10 requires multi-factor authentication for any role able to approve a compliance gate; DDP has none today, so a single password is all that stands between an attacker and the ability to override the export gate -- the one action that lets product move against a failed check. Enforcement is real and wired in as a BEFORE INSERT trigger on export_gate_overrides (a trigger, not a check inside an RPC, so it holds no matter which code path writes the row, including the SQL editor). It ships DISABLED because enabling it before any administrator has enrolled a second factor would lock every approver out at once, turning a security improvement into an outage. A MISSING settings row means REQUIRED, not disabled: deleting a row must never be a way to switch off a control, since that is the edit an attacker reaches for and the one an operator makes by accident.

verify.note: C and D are a matched pair: C proves the migration ships disabled so applying it cannot lock anyone out, D proves enforcement actually bites once switched on. Either alone would be misleading -- C on its own describes a control that does nothing, D on its own describes one that causes an outage on install. E is the section most likely to be got backwards elsewhere: it deletes the settings row and asserts enforcement defaults to REQUIRED, because the failure mode of the opposite default is silent (nobody notices a gate that stopped checking) while this one is loud and recoverable. B checks both JWT transports Supabase has used, since reading only one would make aal2 permanently unsatisfiable and the gate unusable once enabled. NOT read-only; wrapped in BEGIN..ROLLBACK.
